legend: Note the morula-like and hollow clusters of cancer cells immersed in empty stromal spaces.
The unique pattern of polarity is best appreciated with EMA (MUC1) staining lining the peripheral cell membrane facing the stroma, confirming the inside-out growth pattern.

Note the cell clusters with cuboidal to columnar neoplastic cells devoid of a fibrovascular core. The cell clusters display an inside-out growth pattern and are immersed in empty stromal spaces surrounded by a delicate stromal framework composed of fibroblasts and connective tissue.
Strong and complete membranous immunohistochemical staining (score 3+) for ERBB2 (HER2).

diagnosis: Invasive carcinoma with micropapillary pattern and extracellular mucin
legend: Invasive carcinoma shows a micropapillary pattern with scattered calcifications, accompanied by extracellular mucin that bathes the morular clusters of tumour cells.

diagnosis: Invasive micropapillary carcinoma with apocrine cytomorphology
legend: Invasive micropapillary carcinoma consists of clusters of carcinoma cells within clear cleft-like spaces. In this case the cells have apocrine morphology, abundant cytoplasm, and high-grade nuclei. A psammomatous calcification is present. (H&E)

diagnosis: Invasive micropapillary carcinoma: ERBB2 (HER2) 2+ staining (basolateral pattern)
legend: The clusters of this invasive carcinoma express HER2 in a basolateral (U-shaped) distribution. This staining pattern is classified as HER2 2+ (equivocal) and mandates HER2 FISH testing.

diagnosis: Invasive micropapillary carcinoma with apocrine morphology
legend: The invasive micropapillary carcinoma consists of small tight clusters of carcinoma cells with apocrine morphology present within clear cleft-like spaces.
Morula-like and hollow clusters of cancer cells are immersed in empty stromal spaces.
High magnification shows that the cuboidal to columnar neoplastic cells exhibit an inside-out growth pattern, without a fibrovascular core. Clear and empty spaces are seen around the cell clusters.

Cell clusters with cuboidal to columnar neoplastic cells devoid of a fibrovascular core. The cell clusters display an inside-out growth pattern and are immersed in empty stromal spaces surrounded by a delicate stromal framework composed of fibroblasts and connective tissue.

Core biopsy shows mucinous carcinoma admixed with invasive micropapillary carcinoma, the latter seen in the fibrous stroma as micropapillary tumour nests within clear empty spaces. The mucinous component also shows micropapillary nests suspended within mucin.

Invasive micropapillary carcinoma consists of small tight clusters of carcinoma cells within clear cleft-like spaces. The cells at the periphery of the clusters show reverse polarity with the apical cytoplasmic compartment facing towards the peripheral clear space.

Invasive micropapillary carcinoma consists of small tight clusters of carcinoma cells within clear cleft-like spaces. The cells at the periphery of the clusters show reverse polarity with the apical cytoplasmic compartment facing towards the peripheral clear space. DCIS of intermediate nuclear grade with comedo necrosis is also present.
